races.name: Edinburgh Gin Rhubarb And Ginger Handicap

runners_data.name: Albegone
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse facing traffic problems with most rivals also coming from behind
runners_data.comment: On a dangerous mark but drying conditions wouldn't be in his favour
runners_data.spotlight: Finished behind Wee Mary when fifth of ten at Carlisle last week; best on good or slower ground so wouldn't be ideally suited by drying conditions.

runners_data.name: Wrestling Revenue
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but recent front-running effort at Ripon suggests tactical versatility
runners_data.spotlight: Slipped to a good mark and there was much more encouragement from him at Ripon nine days ago, making the running and beaten just over 2l at the finish; one to consider, especially if backed.

runners_data.name: Wee Mary
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in good current form but drawn into a pace scenario that doesn't suit
runners_data.comment: Infrequent winner but she arrives in good form and should be in the thick of it again
runners_data.spotlight: Just one win to her name but she comes here in good order, most recently bumping into a well-handicapped opponent at Hamilton eight days ago (5f, good); should be in the thick of it again.

runners_data.name: Royal Duke
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong course record but moderate recent efforts after 16-day break
runners_data.comment: Two-time C&D winner; on a good mark but yet to shine so far this year
runners_data.spotlight: Two of his three wins have come over C&D, the latest last August off a 4lb higher mark; not found his best in two runs this year but he's the type to pop up at some point.

runners_data.name: Classy Clarets
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid recent form but faces tactical disadvantage in this pace setup
runners_data.comment: Two wins this year and latest C&D second was a good effort; solid contender
runners_data.spotlight: Two wins for Iain Jardine this year, the latest at Hamilton last month off a 3lb lower mark; good second over C&D 16 days ago; more appealing than most.

runners_data.name: Fear And Fast
runners_data.note: Key pace angle as the main front-runner, switching from visor to hood today
runners_data.comment: 0-18 and he's finished last in both runs this year; change of headgear today; not solid
runners_data.spotlight: 18-race maiden; dropping down the weights but his two runs this year have seen him finish last at Ayr and over C&D; hood replaces a visor today; likely to pop up at some point but stable have more obvious claims with Wee Mary.

runners_data.name: Sixcor
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who could provide early company but trainer out of form
runners_data.comment: Conditions no problem but neither run last month suggested he was the answer here
runners_data.spotlight: Conditions no issue but neither run last month suggested he was the answer to today's puzzle.

runners_data.name: Hard Nut
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 213-day layoff with trainer struggling for winners
runners_data.comment: Just one win since July 2019; easy to swerve after 213 days off
runners_data.spotlight: His only win since July 2019 came over this C&D but it is easy enough to look elsewhere now he returns from a 213-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Fear And Fast will make the running with only Sixcor as potential early company, setting up a sustainable pace without early pressure in this small field. The majority of runners (Albegone, Wrestling Revenue, Wee Mary, Royal Duke, Classy Clarets, Hard Nut) are hold-up horses who will settle behind and need to be wound up for their runs. With limited pace pressure and most horses needing to come from off the pace, this race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems. The tactical verdict clearly favours those racing on or close to the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Fear And Fast gets an easy lead without pressure from Sixcor
scenarios.body: Fear And Fast will dictate fractions and prove hard to peg back with so many hold-up horses queuing behind him. The lack of pace pressure allows him to reserve energy for the finish while the hold-up brigade face traffic problems.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely slow and bunches the field
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get their ideal scenario with a sprint finish where superior class can tell. Classy Clarets and Wrestling Revenue benefit most from a truly-run finish where their recent form edge shows.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Drama
scenarios.trigger: If Fear And Fast stops quickly in the final furlong after leading
scenarios.body: Sixcor inherits the lead while the hold-up horses are caught flat-footed too far back. The prominent runner benefits from being closer to the pace when the leader falters.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Course Specialist Returns
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Duke rediscovers his best form at this favourite track
scenarios.body: His two course wins give him the edge despite moderate recent efforts, exploiting local knowledge. The 213-day absence of Hard Nut makes course form less reliable for others.

watchPoints.text: Fear And Fast breaking slowly would leave this race without any genuine pace
Wrestling Revenue's positioning early - if he tracks the pace rather than settling behind
Sixcor's willingness to race prominently rather than dropping back into the pack
The pace in the opening two furlongs - if genuinely slow it changes the entire complexion
Royal Duke for signs of a return to his course-winning form despite the long absence

races.name: Edinburgh Gin Hugo Spritz Selling Stakes

runners_data.name: Tango Hotel
runners_data.note: Prominent type with potential untapped ability, 52 days off may have sharpened her up for smart connections
runners_data.comment: Debut fourth has been franked since; drops into a seller and can do much better
runners_data.spotlight: No match for a smart filly on her Beverley debut in April (5f, good to soft) but it was still a fair run and the form has received some boosts; could be capable of a fair bit better.

runners_data.name: Furturra
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner with strong C&D form, represents in-form Tim Easterby stable with David Allan's tactical nous
runners_data.comment: Placed on his last two starts, including C&D; leading form claims once again; yard run two
runners_data.spotlight: Finished second in a C&D maiden last month; similar form when third in a 6f seller at Chester last week; solid claims once again for a stable also represented by Turnstile.

runners_data.name: Havana Gift
runners_data.note: Failed to build on debut promise, needs significant improvement but prominent style fits race shape
runners_data.comment: Her Thirsk debut was OK but failed to build on it on AW 11 days later; improvement needed
runners_data.spotlight: Her Thirsk debut wasn't without encouragement but she failed to build on it at Southwell 11 days later; improvement essential.

runners_data.name: Dee's Star
runners_data.note: Showed speed in novice events, dropping to selling grade should find easier opportunities from prominent position
runners_data.comment: She has shown enough in two fillies' novices to give her a shout now dropped into a seller
runners_data.spotlight: She has shown some speed in a couple of 5f fillies' novice events to date, finishing in midfield on both occasions; drops into a seller and should have a more realistic chance today.

runners_data.name: Needin' U
runners_data.note: Faded badly on debut over 6f but early pace shown suggests 5f drop could help, lowest rated runner
runners_data.comment: Market springer on Redcar debut (6f, good) but dropped away late on; down in trip/grade
runners_data.spotlight: 16-1 into 4-1 ahead of her Redcar debut 19 days ago (6f, good) but having shown some pace she dropped away in the final furlong; down to 5f/selling company so interesting to see if her supporters return.

runners_data.name: Tree Wizard
runners_data.note: Only front runner with cheekpieces fitted after improved second at Beverley, perfectly positioned to exploit lack of pace pressure
runners_data.comment: Second in Beverley claimer on latest start; can do better but the needs to if he's to win
runners_data.spotlight: Down the field in a 5f maiden at Bath on debut; improved when second of seven in a Beverley claimer ten days ago (5f, good to firm; cheekpieces on for the first time); further progress will be required but it is not out of the question.

runners_data.name: Turnstile
runners_data.note: Returns to preferred 5f trip with valuable rail draw, prominent style suits anticipated pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Not at his best over 6f last time; down into a seller and looks a key player back at 5f
runners_data.spotlight: No improvement for 6f on his last two starts; shouldn't be inconvenienced by returning to 5f and he has the rail to help him; one of two leading contenders for Tim Easterby.

races.paceDynamic: Tree Wizard will take the field along from the start as the only confirmed front runner, likely getting an uncontested lead in this small field of seven. The rest - Furturra, Tango Hotel, Havana Gift, Dee's Star, Turnstile, and Needin' U - are all prominent racers who will settle just behind rather than challenge Tree Wizard early. With no genuine pace pressure expected, Tree Wizard can dictate fractions and kick clear when ready. This setup strongly favours the leader and any prominent runners with a turn of foot, as they'll get ideal positioning without having to work hard early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tree Wizard Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Tree Wizard breaks cleanly and faces no early pressure from the prominent pack
scenarios.body: He can steal several lengths turning for home before the field realizes the danger, holding off late challenges with his uncontested advantage. His recent second at Beverley in similar conditions shows he has the tactical speed to exploit this scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners track Tree Wizard closely and produce a sustained drive from the 2f pole
scenarios.body: Furturra and Turnstile can use their superior ratings and recent form to reel in the leader, with the pace honest enough to set up their finishing kicks. Both have shown they can win from prominent positions at this trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Kick
scenarios.trigger: If Tree Wizard sets modest fractions and the field remains bunched approaching the final furlong
scenarios.body: Tango Hotel could benefit from the patient ride that Oisin Orr can provide, timing her challenge perfectly as others fade. Her debut form suggests untapped ability that could surface in this weaker grade.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Tree Wizard goes too slowly early and stops in the final 100 yards after the prominent pack converges
scenarios.body: Even Needin' U could get involved despite her poor debut, as the race becomes a sprint finish where her early speed might just carry her through. This chaos scenario opens the door for any horse with residual pace.

watchPoints.text: Tree Wizard breaking slowly would completely change the pace dynamic as no other confirmed leaders exist
Furturra settling too far back early given his best form comes from tracking the pace closely
Needin' U's market moves after being well-backed on debut before disappointing
Any prominent runner showing reluctance to take up position behind Tree Wizard could create unexpected pressure
Pierre-Louis Jamin's handling of Tree Wizard in the early stages as the Frenchman rides the presumed pace-setter

races.name: Edinburgh Gin Classic Handicap

runners_data.name: Royalty Bay
runners_data.note: Lone pace-setter returning after 41 days with underwhelming recent form, vulnerable to being swamped late
runners_data.comment: Last year was mostly underwhelming and so too her comeback effort over C&D
runners_data.spotlight: Should be on a good mark but last year was mostly underwhelming and so too her comeback effort over C&D; opposable.

runners_data.name: Modern Times
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse drawn in stall 1 who can race prominently, David Allan booking significant with Easterby's 7/98 record
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden winner who has had lots of chances in handicaps but ran well to be sixth of 22 at York (good), running on over 7f; drawn in 1 and can race prominently; considered.

runners_data.name: Zubaru
runners_data.note: Strong recent winner stepping up 1lb, drawn wide but proven finisher over this trip on good ground
runners_data.comment: Handicap mark has taken a hit but he's still hard to knock in current form
runners_data.spotlight: Mark took a hit for back-to-back wins (7f, good to firm) but only went down by a head at Yarmouth and now just 1lb higher; hard to knock, other than being drawn wide.

runners_data.name: Abduction
runners_data.note: Course and distance winner in April, better over 7f than 6f, Jim Goldie's dual runner suggests confidence
runners_data.comment: C&D winner in April and ran pretty well last time at Hamilton as 6f is too sharp
runners_data.spotlight: Multiple winner who won over C&D in April and ran pretty well last time at Hamilton as 6f is too sharp these days; still on a competitive mark; chance.

runners_data.name: Society Man
runners_data.note: Inconsistent performer returning after 49 days, best efforts have come on artificial surfaces
runners_data.spotlight: His best efforts in Britain have been on AW and he was ideally suited by testing ground when trained in France; none too consistent, either.

runners_data.name: Yaaser
runners_data.note: Veteran campaigner with reduced rating but poor recent form, second string for in-form Goldie yard
runners_data.comment: Won over this trip on the AW in December but has been out the back in subsequent races
runners_data.spotlight: Won over this trip on the AW in December but has been out the back in subsequent races.

runners_data.name: Black Storm
runners_data.note: Consistent sort after wind surgery, suited by 7f trip and represents small trainer in form
runners_data.comment: AW winner in Ireland; mostly consistent in defeat for current yard; this is his trip
runners_data.spotlight: AW winner in Ireland; mostly consistent in defeat for current yard, after wind surgery in last two races; this is his trip and unlikely to be too far away.

runners_data.name: Mae Amor
runners_data.note: Six furlong specialist stepping up in trip with 7lb claimer, yet to prove effectiveness beyond sprint distances
runners_data.comment: Won in May but never going at York a week later; has done all his winning at 6f
runners_data.spotlight: Only scraped home by a short head at Hamilton (6f) last month and was never in contention at York the following week; has done all his winning at 6f and yet to shine over 7f.

runners_data.name: Wreck It Ryley
runners_data.note: One-time winner this year but struggling since, trainer Alan Brown has poor recent record at 0/5
runners_data.comment: He's not looked well handicapped since scoring by 6l in April; also better at 6f
runners_data.spotlight: Kept trying when third at Doncaster last time (6f) but was beaten over 3l and he's not looked well handicapped since scoring by 6l in April; he's also only 1-16 over 7f.

races.paceDynamic: Royalty Bay is the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate terms from the start without early pressure. With eight hold-up horses behind her, this creates a tactical race where the leaders get first run but face a wall of late challengers. The pace will be sustainable early before quickening from 2f out as the field bunches up. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track Royalty Bay and get first run, as pure hold-up horses will struggle to make up ground against the numbers ahead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Duo Control
scenarios.trigger: If Royalty Bay and Modern Times establish a clear lead and aren't caught napping.
scenarios.body: The front two get optimal splits and kick clear before the hold-up brigade can organize their challenge. Modern Times benefits from his prominent style and David Allan's tactical nous.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Charge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses and the field comes to Royalty Bay en masse.
scenarios.body: The leaders fold under pressure as multiple hold-up horses converge simultaneously from the back. Zubaru's proven finishing kick and recent form edge gives him the advantage in a driving finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Muddle
scenarios.trigger: If jockeys get caught in a slow early pace war and sprint finish ensues.
scenarios.body: The race becomes scrappy with multiple horses vying for position turning in, creating traffic problems. Black Storm's consistency and Katie Scott's small but effective stable gives him the edge in the scramble.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Ambush
scenarios.trigger: If the market leaders underperform and a longshot capitalizes on the tactical nature.
scenarios.body: The race unfolds to suit an unfancied runner who gets the perfect trip through the chaos. Yaaser's reduced rating and Jim Goldie's 7/41 strike rate suggests stable form, while his hold-up style could benefit from others' tactical errors.

watchPoints.text: Royalty Bay could get an uncontested lead if Modern Times doesn't press forward early from stall 1
Zubaru drawn in stall 9 may struggle to get into contention if the pace is strong and field stays together
Jim Goldie runs two with Abduction looking the stronger option over Yaaser on recent evidence
Several hold-up horses with 7lb+ claiming jockeys could get outpaced if this becomes tactical
Modern Times switching from 6f to 7f could be the key move with David Allan taking the ride

races.name: Edinburgh Gin Queen Of Scots British EBF Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: La Brodeuse
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits but 28 days off and stepping up to Listed level after just one run for new connections creates questions
runners_data.comment: Well-backed runner-up on stable debut in Group 3 at Lingfield; leading claims on that form
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced French winner (1m, soft) who, after changing hands for 125,000euros, was a well-backed runner-up on her stable and seasonal debut in the Group 3 Chartwell Stakes at Lingfield (7f, good to firm) four weeks ago; leading claims if confirming that promise this afternoon.

runners_data.name: Circe
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 190-day break but has strong Listed race experience and three wins on similar going
runners_data.comment: Went off the boil at the end of last term but can be in the mix if she's back to her best
runners_data.spotlight: Went off the boil in Listed races at the end of last season; however, a break may have helped and she was progressive last term, with three handicap wins (6f, good/good to firm) and a good fourth of 18 in the Group 3 Sceptre Stakes at Doncaster (7f, soft); can be in the mix if she's back to her best.

runners_data.name: Havana Pusey
runners_data.note: Natural leader who should get uncontested lead and has solid recent Group 3 form over this distance
runners_data.comment: Group 3 third at Lingfield four weeks ago and she could be thereabouts
runners_data.spotlight: Won a handicap at Yarmouth (7f, good) in April and another big run, despite an awkward start, when third in the Group 3 Chartwell Stakes at Lingfield last month (7f, good to firm; 1l behind runner-up Magic Basma); also effective on good to soft (yet to run well on soft); she could be thereabouts.

runners_data.name: Figjam
runners_data.note: Prominent 3yo getting 10lb allowance but only 15 days since last run and stepping back up in class
runners_data.comment: Behind Magic Basma when Listed fourth at Haydock but today's extra furlong could help
runners_data.spotlight: Promising 2yo last season, finishing second in a Listed race at Doncaster (6f, heavy) in October; respectable seventh in the Group 3 Fred Darling at Newbury (7f, good) on reappearance and fourth of 15 in Listed race at Haydock (6f, good to soft) a fortnight ago, about 4l behind the runner-up Magic Basma; shaped last time as though the return to 7f could help; not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Golden Palace
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who needs strong pace but looked in need of her reappearance run 52 days ago
runners_data.comment: Could improved for her comeback in the Nell Gwyn but others have more substance to claims
runners_data.spotlight: Kept on for fifth of 19 in 2yo Listed race at Newmarket (6f, good) last October and she could be sharper for her reappearance run there in April (7f, good), when seventh in the Group 3 Nell Gwyn; however, others have more substance to their claims.

runners_data.name: Magic Basma
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with improved Listed form this year but has never won beyond 6f which raises distance concerns
runners_data.comment: Return to 7f poses a question but major player on this year's improved 6f Listed form
runners_data.spotlight: 4yo who has shown improved form in Listed races this term, finishing fourth at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) and runner-up at Haydock (6f, good to soft); she's 0-11 since her debut win in August 2024 and the return to 7f poses a question, but this is an easy track and she's a major player on form.

runners_data.name: Brazilian Rose
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with strong AW form but 0-6 on turf and needs significant class improvement
runners_data.comment: Four AW handicaps this year but needs sizeable step forward to pose a threat in this
runners_data.spotlight: Four handicap wins on the Southwell AW this January-March (7f/6f) and has also shown promise on turf (albeit 0-6 on grass); however, she needs a sizeable step forward if she's to pose a threat in this Listed contest.

runners_data.name: Beaujolais Nouveau
runners_data.note: Prominent runner wearing cheekpieces for second time after breakthrough Ripon win 20 days ago
runners_data.comment: Convincing handicap win at Ripon last time but something to find back into Listed race
runners_data.spotlight: Returned to her best when winning a handicap with something to spare in first-time cheekpieces at Ripon (6f, good) three weeks ago; also effective at 7f and she could have more to offer in the retained headgear, but she has something to find back into a Listed race.

races.paceDynamic: Havana Pusey will lead from the gate with Circe, Figjam and Beaujolais Nouveau tracking closely behind in the opening furlongs. The pace should be genuine but not frantic with only one confirmed front runner, allowing the prominent runners to settle comfortably. Magic Basma, La Brodeuse and Golden Palace will drop towards the rear from their hold-up styles. This sustainable early tempo followed by tactical positioning battles in the final 2f clearly favours prominent racers who can track the pace and kick when it matters.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays honest but manageable through halfway
scenarios.body: Havana Pusey and Circe can dictate terms without pressure, while Figjam travels smoothly in their slipstream ready to pounce. The hold-up horses find too much traffic and insufficient pace collapse to mount their challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group goes too hard trying to collar Havana Pusey
scenarios.body: Magic Basma and La Brodeuse benefit from a strong pace that sets up their closing kicks perfectly over the final furlong. Golden Palace could also get into the mix if the pace truly collapses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If jockeys get cute and nobody wants to commit early
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the 2f pole where class tells and Circe's experience in Listed company proves decisive. Figjam's 3yo allowance becomes crucial in a slowly-run affair.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Surprises
scenarios.trigger: If the market leaders fail to fire on the day
scenarios.body: Brazilian Rose's recent AW form translates to turf or Beaujolais Nouveau's cheekpieces continue to work their magic from her Ripon success. Golden Palace could also benefit from being fresher than most.

watchPoints.text: Havana Pusey breaks slowly again like at Lingfield as any tardy start could compromise her front-running tactics
Magic Basma gets shuffled back too far given her 0-7 record at 7f and preference for shorter trips
Circe shows signs of needing the run after her 190-day absence despite her class advantage
La Brodeuse struggles to adapt to British racing tactics in just her second start for Kevin Ryan
Brazilian Rose handles the switch from all-weather to turf for the first time this season

races.name: Edinburgh Cup Handicap

runners_data.name: Haayimm
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has shown smart form when getting the run of the race and benefits from 34 days freshening up
runners_data.comment: Pushed a promising horse close last time and brings potential into handicaps
runners_data.spotlight: Gelded after one run last season; floored the 1-8 favourite (who has since disappointed again) in a maiden at Pontefract and then pushed another market leader (promising gelding) close over Hamilton's extended 1m (good); finished that race out well after getting outpaced and a truer-run contest here would suit on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Evening Blues
runners_data.note: Prominent runner switching from all-weather to turf with headgear applied, representing an in-form trainer
runners_data.comment: Close fifth at Wetherby and the hood that worked well for him in Ireland now returns
runners_data.spotlight: AW winner for Ger Lyons, for whom he was 1-7; weak in the betting when fifth of 11 on yard debut at Wetherby but, although he wasn't beaten far, that was a Class 4; the hood that worked well for him in Ireland now returns.

runners_data.name: Monoceros
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who joined Iain Jardine for decent money and showed promise when third behind Strength Of Spirit recently
runners_data.comment: Useful for Godolphin and still lightly raced; likeable stable debut when third here
runners_data.spotlight: Pulled up on his final run for Godolphin but his first two efforts read well; joined current yard for 25,000gns and kept on takingly for third behind Strength Of Spirit over 1m here in April (handicap debut); open to improvement.

runners_data.name: Strength Of Spirit
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose progress has stalled but has course form and relatively fresh having run just 14 days ago
runners_data.comment: Three wins but progress has stalled, markedly so in his last two races
runners_data.spotlight: Has done well for one who opened his account in a seller, bagging his second handicap over 1m here in April; however, progress has stalled, markedly so in his last two races (competitive ones admittedly).

runners_data.name: Magical Merlot
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who was gelded over winter and showed improved form when third at Windsor last time
runners_data.comment: Recent Windsor third; could step up again but will need to in this better race
runners_data.spotlight: Brighton novice winner last season at 1m; gelded in November; perhaps needed his first run back and then he stuck on gamely for a close third at Windsor (1m, good to firm); could step up again but will need to in this better race.

runners_data.name: Blues And Royals
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who hit traffic problems at Sandown and drops back from that higher grade
runners_data.comment: Dual AW winner and Sandown last time didn't go entirely to plan; remains of interest
runners_data.spotlight: Maintained his progress when repelling Victory Ace for a second AW success in May (1m) and Sandown last time didn't go entirely to plan after hitting traffic; remains of interest.

runners_data.name: Victory Ace
runners_data.note: Another hold-up performer who does his best work late and has been closing strongly in recent starts
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced gelding who is improving steadily and he's raised again in distance
runners_data.spotlight: Picked up from Roger Varian for 40,000gns; edged home on his handicap debut over 7f and again did his best work late at Kempton (1m) when closing in on Blues And Royals with whom he's closely matched; goes further again here with little weight to carry and he has to be feared.

runners_data.name: Pandemonium
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner whose two tailed-off efforts this year raise serious concerns about his well-being
runners_data.comment: Won his first two races but desperate since; now gelded and tried in cheekpieces
runners_data.spotlight: Last year's two wins were over 7f on soft/good to soft before finishing tailed off in a Group 2; he worryingly suffered the same fate on handicap debut at the Craven meeting (1m, good) since when he's been gelded; has a few questions to answer now and the cheekpieces are new.

races.paceDynamic: Pandemonium is the sole confirmed front-runner in this field and will be allowed to dictate terms uncontested in the early stages. The prominent runners Evening Blues and Strength Of Spirit will track him at a respectful distance, while the large contingent of hold-up horses (Haayimm, Monoceros, Magical Merlot, Blues And Royals, Victory Ace) will settle towards the rear. This creates a classic scenario where the pace-setter gets an easy time of it early before the closers launch their challenge in the straight. The race shape strongly favours the hold-up horses who will benefit from the uncontested gallop and have plenty to aim at in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Brigade Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Pandemonium sets a steady gallop that suits the closers
scenarios.body: The large group of hold-up horses will have the perfect target to aim at and can time their runs to perfection. With five quality closers in the field, they will swamp the leaders in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals March
scenarios.trigger: If Pandemonium gets away with a very soft lead and kicks clear
scenarios.body: Despite his poor recent form, he could exploit the tactical setup if the hold-up horses leave it too late. The lack of early pressure plays into his hands perfectly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Evening Blues and Strength Of Spirit position closer to the pace
scenarios.body: They can bridge the gap between Pandemonium and the hold-up horses, getting first run on the closers. Their more forward positioning gives them a tactical edge over the rear division.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Pandemonium goes too slow and kicks too late
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where any horse can win regardless of running style. Form and class become secondary to who gets the best run in a messy finish.

watchPoints.text: Pandemonium's recent form is alarming with two tailed-off efforts - if he shows early signs of distress, the race shape changes completely

races.paceDynamic: Merlier is the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate terms from the gate with no pressure for the lead. Major Neigh Sayer, Mighty Magnus, Arduis Invicta, and Lebron Power will likely track in prominent positions behind the leader, creating a bunched field through the early stages. The sustainable pace Merlier sets will keep the field compact turning for home, setting up a sprint finish over the final furlong. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track the pace and kick, rather than hold-up horses who need a strong gallop to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Merlier Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Merlier gets an uncontested lead and maintains steady fractions.
scenarios.body: The cheekpiece addition helps him focus and he has enough in reserve to hold off late challengers in a race run to suit front-runners. His recent Beverley seller win shows he retains ability despite the class rise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes just quick enough to soften up Merlier in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Major Neigh Sayer or Mighty Magnus can utilize their tactical speed from prominent positions to strike when Merlier weakens. The good going suits both horses' recent form patterns.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is slower than expected, creating a sprint finish from deep.
scenarios.body: Kind Touch's hold-up style becomes viable in a truly-run sprint where his late kick can be effective from off the pace. His debut win showed he possesses a turn of foot when getting the right race shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the market principals fail to fire and an improving sort capitalizes.
scenarios.body: Dandy Breeze bounces back from his turf debut disappointment or Arduis Invicta continues her consistent handicap form at a favorable weight. The competitive nature of the handicap allows for surprises from horses with less obvious claims.

races.paceDynamic: Nakatomi and On The Bubble will likely set a measured pace early, with Freak Encounter also showing prominent tendencies but less reliable. The lack of confirmed speed horses suggests a steady gallop rather than fierce early pace, allowing the field to stay compact through the first half-mile. This sets up a tactical finish where stamina and positioning become crucial over sustained effort. Hold-up horses with proven staying power will benefit most from this scenario, as they can settle and unleash late kicks against a pace that won't string out the field early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace remains steady as expected
scenarios.body: The compact field allows hold-up specialists like Little Ted, War Memorial and Monhammer to settle perfectly before delivering strong late challenges. Their superior class and stamina prove decisive in a finish where positioning matters more than early speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Nakatomi and On The Bubble go too slowly early
scenarios.body: The crawling pace becomes a sprint finish where any horse can win from anywhere, favouring those with tactical speed regardless of usual style. Fresh horses and good jockeys become paramount in a bunched finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Control
scenarios.trigger: If On The Bubble and Nakatomi maintain ideal positions throughout
scenarios.body: The race becomes a test of who can best combine early positioning with late acceleration. Those tracking the pace closely gain crucial tactical advantages over hold-up horses caught too far back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens unexpectedly and tests stamina fully
scenarios.body: The genuine stayers emerge from the pack as lesser horses fade, creating opportunities for unfancied but consistent types. Distance specialists who handle the step up in trip prove their worth.
